felicitous

/fih-LIS-ih-tuhs/ - the stress falls on LIS · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Felicitous means strikingly well suited, with a glow of happy luck about the fit.

Her felicitous nickname for the wobbling robot — 'Sir Stumbles' — stuck within the hour.

Example

Asked to caption the yearbook photo of the flooded gymnasium, Rosa wrote 'Swim Team Tryouts,' a felicitous two words that said everything the four-paragraph article beside it had struggled to say.

Felicitous is stronger than 'fitting' because it carries a spark of happy luck—the phrase or choice lands so well that it feels both perfectly suited and delightfully unforced.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

apt: Apt means exactly to the point — an apt remark hits its target cleanly and stops there. Felicitous starts from that same accuracy and adds a glow of happy luck: a felicitous phrase feels not only right but delightfully unforced, as if the fit itself were good fortune.

fitting: Fitting means suitable in a plain, dutiful way — a fitting tribute meets the occasion's requirements and nothing more. Felicitous praise goes further: a felicitous choice does not merely meet the requirement, it lands with a spark of charm that makes the fit itself a pleasure.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

clumsy: handled without skill or grace

graceless: landing badly, with no charm in the choice

Where it sits · how brilliantly the choice fits — suitable → felicitous → inspired

suitable vs. felicitous: Suitable stops short of felicitous — a suitable phrase does its job without delighting anyone.

inspired vs. felicitous: Inspired goes further than felicitous — an inspired choice feels like a small stroke of genius no one else could have found.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — felicit-

Root — felicit-: happiness, good luck (Latin felicitas)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: full of

Put it together

Put it together: Felicit- (happiness, good luck) + -ous (full of) = full of happy luck. Latin felix meant both happy and lucky, and felicitous keeps the double meaning: a felicitous phrase is one that fits so well it seems to have arrived by good fortune.

Use the root in a new word: felicity

Use the root in a new word: felicity: Editors kept quoting the felicity of her closing sentence for weeks afterward.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Felicitous belongs to reviews, toasts, and essays — praise for a choice of words, a name, a pairing that lands perfectly. For everyday praise, 'spot-on' or 'well chosen' is plainer; reach for felicitous when the fit itself deserves applause.
